subject: Storix: deployment criteria & ops plan — throughput/latency confirmation
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@storix.ai>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.s@storix.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — follow-up and clarification on throughput/latency goals

Kimberly, thanks again for the demo and the conversation earlier today — good to meet the Redwood team. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so your engineering team can size an accurate POC.

High-level pains we called out:
- Large variance in inference latency during peak periods (p99 spikes from ~200ms to >900ms).
- Cost unpredictability when traffic bursts; current provider charges explode with auto-scale.
- Need for private-control plane / VPC deployment because of data residency and compliance.

What we said we need (please confirm if Redwood can meet these):
1) Latency SLO: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 350ms for a 512-token completion on our primary model (Llama-70B equivalent, quantized).
2) Sustained throughput: baseline of 180 concurrent sustained RPCs (average gen length ~350 tokens), with 400 concurrent burst capacity for up to 10 minutes.
3) Model constraints: 70B model, prefer 4-bit quant with offload options; support for KV cache warm start during rollouts.
4) Deployment topology: private VPC with dedicated capacity in a single AWS region (us-west-2), multi-AZ preferred for failover.
5) Observability & compliance: token-level cost breakdowns, request tracing, and audit logs (SOC2 evidence required).
6) Procurement timeline: target production in 8–10 weeks if POC ok — procurement/contracting will be handled by Priya (cc).

Can you confirm which of the above is achievable out-of-the-box vs. requires Dedicated/Private? If possible, please include an initial estimate of GPU capacity and a rough cost delta for Dedicated vs hosted fallback. Also, we attached a simple workload profile and a network diagram we use for procurement — these should help.

Happy to hop back on a technical deep-dive next week — availability is Wed/Thu afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of ML Ops | Storix

Alex — really helpful write-up, thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise recap from Redwood, plus proposed next steps & POC acceptance criteria so everyone has alignment.

Redwood recap (what we believe you asked for):
- Target SLOs: p99 <= 350ms for 512 tokens (we can tune kernel/batching to target this; p95/p50 margins are straightforward).
- Throughput: baseline 180 concurrent RPCs; support bursting to 400 for short windows.
- Model: 70B family supported. We recommend 4-bit QAT or GPTQ-style post-training quant for best latency/cost tradeoff; offload to host memory if necessary.
- Topology: Private deployment (Redwood Private) in us-west-2 with a Dedicated GPU pool, multi-AZ replicas and automated failover to a smaller hosted pool for non-sensitive traffic if desired.
- Observability: token-level cost, per-route latency/trace, and audit logs (we can provide SOC2 artifacts as part of enterprise onboarding).

POC acceptance criteria (suggested):
1) Sustained p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 350ms under a 180-concurrent synthetic workload with generation length 350 tokens.
2) Controlled 10-minute burst to 400 concurrent with no more than 2x degradation in p99 latency.
3) End-to-end tracing enabled for 100% of sampled requests and token-cost reporting.
4) KV cache warm start demonstrated on canary model rollout.

Immediate technical suggestions we will include in the deep-dive:
- Serving: continuous batching with max batch ~48 for latency-sensitive endpoints; larger batch off-ramps for background bulk jobs.
- Caching: prefix + KV cache with TTL tuning to handle warm sessions and reduce token recomputation.
- Quant: provide both int4 and int8 profiles; we will run a small benchmark on your sample payload to select the right profile.
- Autoscale policy: reserved baseline capacity + fast vertical scaling for burst windows; suggest keeping a 20% reserved cushion for p99 guarantees.

Attachments (attached to this thread): redwood_cost_estimate.xlsx (estimate with Dedicated vs hosted fallback), our recommended quant/benchmark matrix (we will upload after internal run).

Next steps:
- Please confirm preferred slots for Wed/Thu next week (we'll book a 60-minute deep-dive with Vivek + Marcus included for kernel & capacity planning).
- I'll ask Marcus to produce a first-draft GPU count & cost delta by EOD Thu (internal).
- Vivek will run an internal quick benchmark with a sample of your workload profile to populate quant recommendations.

If any of the items above are misaligned, flag them and we'll adjust.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Kim / Marcus — quick internal follow-up as I review Alex's profile and Kimberly's draft:

Notes / preliminary ops direction:
- Topology: prefer 3 AZ split within us-west-2 for control-plane HA; Dedicated pool sized per AZ with a leader/follower pattern for cache sync.
- Capacity: for baseline 180 concurrent RPCs (avg 350 tokens) I estimate 6 x A100/H100-class GPUs with mixed precision + quantization; for 400 burst target we should plan for warm-burst capacity equivalent to ~12 GPUs (this is rough — Marcus can validate with exact memory footprints).
- Batching: avoid large batch sizes for user-facing RPCs — keep p99-sensitive endpoints max_batch ~32–48 and use per-route overrides.
- Cache: set KV cache TTL to 30 minutes for session-heavy workloads to keep hit rates high across short bursts.

Actions: 
- Marcus: can you produce a GPU count table by Thu EOD (per-quant profile and per-AZ)? Include expected memory usage and estimated latency headroom.
- Me: I'll run an initial quant/throughput probe against the storix_workload_profile.csv today and share results by Fri.
- Kimberly: will you attach the network diagram / any firewall/egress constraints from Storix so the infra team can pre-authorize endpoints?

I'll keep this short — want to make sure we capture these as agenda items for the deep-dive so we don't lose time.

— Vivek
